$schema_note: Local manufacturing knowledge base: deterministic planning rules read by factory.manufacturing.decision_engine. No AI/LLM call - this is reference data plus keyword hints for a deterministic heuristic, mirroring the existing factory/router.py pattern. The engine explains every option below and recommends one; it never silently picks an option or requires anything less than explicit human confirmation.

single_piece.description: Print the whole part as one fused body from one material/color.
advantages: Simplest workflow: one CAD file, one STL, one slicer import, no post-print assembly.
No shared-origin alignment risk between parts.
Fastest to get to slicer_review_ready for straightforward, single-color parts.
disadvantages: Must fit within a single printer's build volume in one orientation.
A single detail failure (e.g. a small broken feature) can require reprinting the entire part.

multipart_build_volume.description: Split a part that is too large for the target printer's build volume into multiple sections printed separately and joined after printing.
advantages: Allows parts larger than any single printer's build plate.
Each section can be reprinted independently if one fails.
disadvantages: Requires designing a joint/alignment feature and post-print assembly.
Seam lines may be visible depending on joint design and material.
Adds assembly effort and a new failure mode (misaligned or weak joints).

multipart_color.description: Export separate aligned STLs per color (e.g. base plate + raised letters) instead of a single fused mesh, per docs/slicer-review-workflow.md.
advantages: Crisp, deliberate per-region color without hand-painting.
Matches this repo's existing multi-part alignment tooling (factory generate-openscad --template multipart-nameplate).
Works well with AMS/AMS 2 Pro-equipped printers for automatic material switching.
disadvantages: Requires an AMS-equipped (or native multi-nozzle) printer for automatic color switching, or manual filament swaps otherwise.
Requires careful shared-origin alignment across all part files.
More manifest/part bookkeeping than a single fused part.

multipart_detail.description: Print fine-detail regions (e.g. small text, thin decorative features) as a separate part, possibly with a smaller nozzle, from the bulk/structural body.
advantages: Lets the detail region use a finer nozzle/slower settings without slowing down the whole print.
Reduces the chance that a bulk-print failure also ruins the fine-detail work.
disadvantages: More parts to align and assemble.
Fine-detail printing is slower per unit area, even isolated to a smaller part.

multipart_paint.description: Split a part so that regions intended for hand-painting are separate, printable in a paint-friendly material (e.g. PLA/ABS/ASA) and maskable/removable during painting.
advantages: Easier to mask adjacent regions and paint cleanly without removing the whole part from its stand/base.
Can choose a more paintable material per region (see config/manufacturing/materials.json paintable flag) instead of one compromise material.
disadvantages: Adds assembly and paint-registration effort (parts must still align after painting).
Some materials chosen for print quality elsewhere (e.g. PETG) are poor for painting - may force a material compromise on that part.

multipart_strength.description: Split a part along load paths so each section can be printed with a stronger orientation/infill/material for its own load case, instead of one compromise orientation for the whole part.
advantages: Each section's print orientation can align layer lines with its actual load direction.
Higher-stress sections can use a stronger material/infill without over-building low-stress sections.
disadvantages: Joints between sections are almost always the weakest point - needs a deliberate joint design (not a simple butt seam) for load-bearing use.
More engineering effort up front; a poor joint design can be weaker than a single-piece print would have been.

replaceable_components.description: Design wear-prone or failure-prone sub-parts (e.g. a clip, a hinge pin, a wear pad) as separate, individually reprintable parts rather than embedding them in the main body.
advantages: A future failure only requires reprinting the small worn/broken sub-part, not the whole assembly.
Encourages parametrizing the sub-part so future revisions (e.g. a tighter fit) don't require redesigning the whole part.
disadvantages: Requires a mechanical interface (screw, clip, press-fit) between the replaceable part and the main body, adding design and tolerancing work.
Slightly more assembly effort than a single fused part.

notes: This file is reference data for factory.manufacturing.decision_engine. It never causes a manufacturing_option to be auto-selected: selected_manufacturing_option in build_plan.json is always null until a human sets it.
advantages/disadvantages text is deliberately generic/reusable; keyword matches only affect which option is recommended, not which options are listed (all options are always listed).
